World Bank estimates put more than 17 million people out of poverty since 2018, and ECLAC's Social Panorama 2026 found that without the universal pension, poverty among adults 65 and over would be 11.5 percentage points higher. "The Revolution left a fundamental lesson: democracy and social justice are inseparable."

🇲🇽🛒 <u>RETAIL SALES DIPPED IN SEPTEMBER, BUT 2026 IS STILL AHEAD OF 2025</u>

According to INEGI data reported by El Economista, retail sales fell 0.3% month over month in September after rising 1.2% in August. They are still up 2.6% from a year earlier, and growth for January–September was 2.8%, compared with 1.9% for the same months of 2025. Retail grew 0.5% in the third quarter, slightly faster than 0.4% in the second. Monex economists said annual growth "remained positive in most segments and in every state."

🇲🇽✈️ <u>CRITICS CALLED THE AIFA A WHITE ELEPHANT. ITS CONSTRUCTION SITE UNCOVERED 13,000 YEARS OF HISTORY</u>

INAH confirmed that Yotzin, the skeleton found in 2021 while the Felipe Ángeles International Airport was being built, is between 13,087 and 11,700 years old, based on two lab analyses in Belgium and at the University of Georgia. He is one of the 23 oldest human skeletons ever found in the Basin of Mexico: a hunter-gatherer about 1.75 m tall, buried among mammoth and prehistoric camel remains. Yotzin means "unique" in Náhuatl.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>NAFTA DROVE THE MIGRATION TRUMP NOW PUNISHES</u>

According to a Contralínea editorial, more than 11 million people of Mexican origin live in the US, and the mass exodus took off after NAFTA came into force in 1994 and left Mexico's farmers competing against heavily subsidized US agribusiness. Migrants make up 17.7% of the US workforce, about 30 million workers. Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico over a caravan of no more than 1,500 people. Sheinbaum replied that Mexico has broken up 24 caravans since 2024. On November 3, Republicans lost the Texas governorship.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>IN MEXICO'S SENATE: US BLOCKADE HAS DOUBLED CUBA'S INFANT MORTALITY</u>

At the 18th Mexico-Cuba Interparliamentary Meeting in Mexico's Senate, Cuban National Assembly vice president Ana María Machado said infant mortality on the island has more than doubled under the US blockade, from 4.4 to 9.9 per 1,000 live births. More than 100,000 patients are waiting for surgery, about 12,000 of them children, while containers of food and medicine sit in foreign ports because shipping companies are threatened. Senate president Higinio Martínez answered that Mexico will keep sending humanitarian aid to Cuba despite outside pressure.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MEXICAN SPECIAL FORCES CAPTURE ONE OF THE FBI'S 10 MOST WANTED</u>

Mexico's Defense Ministry captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, "El Chapo Isidro," head of the Beltrán Leyva cartel, in Guasave, Sinaloa. National Guard "Lobos" and Army "Murciélagos" special forces led the operation, working from intelligence shared under bilateral cooperation, and also arrested his second-in-command "Serafín" and his financial operator. The FBI had put him on its top-ten list in February 2025, with a reward of up to $5 million. In the end, Mexican troops under Mexican command took him down on Mexican soil.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Pemex is refining more and exporting less crude, and the trade balance shows it</u>

Pemex ran a record US$4.835 billion trade deficit from January to September, El Economista reports, as fuel prices spiked after the US military operation in Iran. The model has flipped: crude exports fell 61% to 427,000 bpd while refinery throughput rose 32% to 1.1 million bpd, with Olmeca (Dos Bocas) already processing 17% of the national system's crude. Pemex's debt is down 20% to about $77 billion. Under Peña Nieto it rose 75% to nearly $106 billion while the refineries rotted.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>865 car washes a month, 15 workers, 62 million pesos: ex-PAN mayor Lili Campos arrested</u>

Quintana Roo's prosecutors arrested Roxana Lili Campos, PAN mayor of Solidaridad (Playa del Carmen) from 2021 to 2024, in Mexico City for misuse of authority. Her administration handed three tenders to the same vehicle-wash contractor, which billed up to 865 washes in a single month for a fleet of 123 vehicles, with a staff of 15. The contractor had no tax invoices for the early contracts, and the city kept paying anyway: more than 62 million pesos in unverifiable payments. She had resigned as a CDMX anti-narcomenudeo prosecutor seven days before her arrest.
